findings.title: Faults carried into a petition

findings.containment: The promise is a petition, not a declaration that Jacob has personally erased the offense or that the reunion makes it unreal. The closing names hold forgiveness and mercy together without selecting between them.

findings.title: Mercy through disclosure and guidance
findings.claim: The focus's name of mercy sits within the surah's opening invocation and the story's closing description as lesson, clarification, guidance, and mercy; the ending lets forgiveness open onto mercy that makes a damaged history intelligible.
findings.mechanism: The host basmala already pairs الرحمن الرحيم. At 12:111, the story is called an instruction and detailed clarification before guidance and mercy are named, and the root رحم returns as رحمة. The focus name is thus connected to mercy working through understanding and direction.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive forgiveness as part of a mercy that guides through the story, not only as a disposition toward the offenders.
findings.containment: 12:111 describes the story and revelation for believers; it does not define الرحيم lexically or state that Jacob's petition alone produces every later benefit.

epistemic.reason: The HFT's exact roots and indices match the focus and 12:111; the practical link from the ending to this local name remains an attributed reading.

findings.title: An exploratory image of ongoing care
findings.claim: As an analogy, the future petition can be held as ongoing care for a repaired bond that could be disturbed again.
findings.mechanism: The focus repeats the forgiveness root and leaves the act in the future. In 12:100, Satan's incitement is said to have occurred between brothers; the wound-relapse branch gives that later disturbance a way to meet the focus's promise of protective care.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can imagine forgiveness as care for a relation across time, not as a claim that one successful reconciliation makes future repair unnecessary.
findings.containment: The medical relapse branch is form-distant from ordinary forgiveness. Nothing in the focus denotes illness; the branch supplies an analogy for a relation that may be reopened, and the later verse does not say Jacob's prayer caused repair.

epistemic.reason: The exact trace matches the supplied focus and 12:100, and the dictionary branch is present; applying wound relapse to a family relation remains exploratory.

findings.title: Mercy as protected renewal
findings.claim: The focus places a father's request for his sons beside lordly care and mercy; the family history and its closing guidance allow the petition to be imagined as protected renewal as well as forgiveness.
findings.mechanism: The growth branch under ربي and the containing image available under الرحيم meet the family rupture and reunion in 12:97 and 12:100, then the closing guidance and mercy in 12:111. The attributed child-soothing role adds an exploratory image of re-regulation.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader may perceive the prayer as asking for a future in which the family can be guided into renewed life, not only for a verdict on past conduct.
findings.containment: Growth, womb, and child-soothing are analogies, not lexical translations of ربي, الرحيم, or هدى. The prayer remains a request for forgiveness; the passage does not promise that the sons will be otherwise changed.

epistemic.reason: The focus growth and womb branches have independent packet records, while the HFT-only guidance branches remain attributed. The family and closing context support but do not prove this image.

findings.title: My Lord, Lord of the worlds
findings.claim: Jacob's intimate address to my Lord can be held within the Fatiha's individual description of the same Lord as Lord of the worlds, adding universal scope while keeping the family petition personal.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier ربي meets the separate phrase رب العالمين in 1:2. The added worlds phrase supplies a scale beyond the family's immediate appeal and lets the same lordship be heard across personal and universal scope.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold Jacob's close address and the wider domain of the one addressed together.
findings.containment: This overlay does not turn the family episode into an allegory about all creation or change the possessive force of ربي. It is a scale resonance from the single supplied external ayah.

epistemic.reason: The exact Arabic and root occurrence in 1:2 are supplied; extending its universal scope into the focus is a bounded macro inference.

findings.title: Forgiveness before the Day of Recompense
findings.claim: The focus request for forgiveness can be held beside the Fatiha's description of the Lord as owner of the Day of Recompense, adding a final-accountability horizon to the petition for the brothers' confessed sins.
findings.mechanism: The brothers name their sins in 12:97, and Jacob promises أَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكُمْ رَبِّي in the focus. The individual external ayah 1:4 names the same addressee as مَٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ; the contact lets the request be heard before the one whose sovereignty includes judgment.
findings.reader_payoff: The petition has both its immediate family relation and a horizon of final accountability in view.
findings.containment: 1:4 does not identify the brothers' fate, specify a judgment, or say what result Jacob's petition receives. The overlay adds moral scope while leaving the local request and its uncertainty intact.

epistemic.reason: The confessed sins, focus request, and exact wording of 1:4 are supplied; their relation is a bounded external-context inference.

friction_notes: The focus word alignment resolves all 9 of 9 entries. Supplied HFT context coordinates and roots match the selected occurrence rows; branch claims whose registry is unresolved remain attributed, and the cross-event readings retain their stated alternatives.

Phase 2 retains 1:2 for universal scope and 1:4 for accountability as separate individual-ayah overlays. The remaining additions do not create a distinct local delta: 1:3 repeats the host basmala, 1:5 parallels the petition already in focus, and 1:6-7 add no specific contact beyond the pericope's guidance frame. External context remains ayah-level because no focus QAC join is supplied for it.
